title: A Quick Glance at Assistive Tech 👀
description: Meet the tools people use: screen readers, braille displays, switch devices, and more.

slides.title: Screen Readers 📣
slides.content:
Software that reads the screen aloud. Popular ones:

* **VoiceOver** (macOS/iOS)
* **NVDA** (Windows, free)
* **JAWS** (Windows, paid)
* **TalkBack** (Android)

They interpret the **accessibility tree** – a structured representation of the page.

quizData.question: Which screen reader is built into iPhones?
quizData.explanation: VoiceOver is Apple's screen reader available on all iOS and macOS devices.

slides.title: Other Assistive Technologies 🔌
slides.content:
* **Braille displays**: Refreshable devices that output braille.
* **Screen magnifiers**: Zoom in portions of the screen.
* **Switch devices**: Allow people with limited motor control to interact via single buttons or sip-and-puff.
* **Voice recognition**: Dragon NaturallySpeaking, built‑in dictation.

Your code must work with all of them.

quizData.question: A braille display is a type of screen reader. True or False?
quizData.explanation: A braille display is hardware that outputs braille; a screen reader is software that speaks or sends output to the braille display.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test with Real Assistive Tech

Nothing beats hands‑on testing. Turn on your screen reader and navigate a website using only the keyboard. You'll immediately understand barriers.
